manual.text:
## Specific task description

Task instruction: Stack the three bowls on the table.

Task description: The objects are three light-green bowls scattered on the table. Stack them so they support one another.

Success criteria: By lifting and moving the bowls, stack all three in one pile on the table, with each upper bowl seated and supported inside the lower opening. The complete stack must stand stably on its own.

## Execution tips

- Choose a wall-rim section facing open tabletop, with one finger inside and one outside and pads against the wall below the rim. Match the opening to wall thickness and entry clearance, avoiding a grasp spanning the whole bowl mouth.
- Before closing, use both views to confirm the fingers are inside and outside the bowl wall rather than merely overlapping in the image. Check for slipping or tilt during a small test lift; restore support before adjusting an unstable grasp.
- Keep the bowl opening facing upward during transport, with enough height clearance between its bottom and the rims of other bowls along the way. If its pose needs adjustment, do so in an open area to reduce contact between the rim or gripper and neighboring bowls.
- Align the upper bowl bottom with the lower opening's center and descend in small steps while observing gaps on both sides. If one rim contacts first or the lower bowl shifts, lift slightly and adjust rather than continuing to press inward.
- Watch clearance between the outer finger and lower bowl rim, avoiding trapping fingers between bowls. Once the upper bowl is securely supported, open appropriately and withdraw upward to reduce lifting or toppling the stack.

narration: I will use the piper-control skill to start only this physical-robot episode with the specified parameters, operate from the returned manual and live observations, and call finish_episode upon completion or inability to continue.
The three bowls are separated in the live view. Only the right arm is available. I am adjusting the gripper in an open area and approaching the rim, then will test-lift slightly to check the grasp.

The gripper is confirmed open and is approaching the outer edge of the bowl on the left. Next I will reduce movement increments and close only after confirming that the fingers are on the inside and outside of the bowl wall.

The gripper is aligned with the left bowl rim, and a closure command was sent. I will first check the actual closure state, then test-lift slightly to confirm whether the bowl moves steadily with the gripper.

The first closure did not establish an effective grip, and the bowl remains on the table. I reopened the gripper and am adjusting finger insertion depth and lateral position in steps of no more than 1 cm.
After closing, the gripper retains an actual gap around 10 mm and the image shows the bowl wall between the fingers. I will now test-lift 1 cm to check grasp security.
After the test lift, the gripper gap is stable at about 3.7 mm, and the bowl rose with the gripper, clear of the table. Next I will lift higher for clearance, then move above the other bowl.

The first bowl has been moved above the bowl in front, and the grip remains stable. I am aligning the center of its bottom with the lower bowl opening, then will lower slightly and check whether it is supported.

The upper bowl is gradually entering the front bowl opening, and the lower bowl has not visibly shifted. I will continue checking nesting depth and clearance from the outer finger, then release after confirming support.
The two bowls are nearly aligned and nested. I will descend one final small step, then loosen the gripper moderately and withdraw upward to check whether the stack remains stable on its own.
After release and withdrawal, the two bowls in front remain stably nested. Next I will handle the remaining bowl behind them and place it on the stack.
The right arm is above the outer edge of the remaining bowl, and the front stack remains stable. I am descending gradually to align with the bowl wall, preparing to grasp and test-lift again.
The gripper has descended near the rim of the remaining bowl, with one finger on each side of the wall. Now I will close, check the grasp, and test-lift slightly.

The remaining bowl tilted during a test lift, and stable clearance from the table is not confirmed. The stack of bowls in front shifted slightly but remains nested. I will return this bowl to a supporting surface before adjusting the grasp position.
The bowl has been set down securely again. I adjusted the gripper laterally so the bowl wall is nearer the middle of the fingers and am preparing to increase finger insertion depth before regrasping.
After regrasping, the bowl wall is held more deeply between the fingers. I am testing the lift gradually and checking for slipping; I will transport it after confirming stability.

The gripper gap has stabilized at about 4.9 mm, and the bowl is beginning to rise with the gripper. I will continue lifting slightly, confirming the bowl bottom clears the table and its pose is stable.
The remaining bowl is off the table, and its grasp and pose remain stable. I will maintain overhead clearance, then move above the front bowl stack and complete the final nesting.
The last bowl is above the stack, with its base nearly aligned over the opening below. Next I will descend in small steps, confirm nesting and support, then release.

The tool reported that the operator authorization period cannot cover the next action and returned `done=true`. The third bowl is still held above the stack and has not been released; I will immediately call finish_episode. The on-site operator should take over. The tool has not confirmed a physical stop, and ending the episode does not guarantee holding torque.
